[LoRA] Support modules_to_save for sequence classification (#53555)

Signed-off-by: linitra24 <Joy25810@foxmail.com>

Co-authored-by: Jee Jee Li <pandaleefree@gmail.com>

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide:
This commit adds a new abstract method `apply_lora_full_linear(...)` to `PunicaWrapperABC` (vllm/lora/punica_wrapper/punica_base.py). `PunicaWrapperBase` does NOT provide an implementation — only `PunicaWrapperGPU`, `PunicaWrapperCPU`, and `PunicaWrapperXPU` do. vllm-ascend's `PunicaWrapperNPU` (vllm_ascend/lora/punica_npu.py:16) inherits `PunicaWrapperBase` and does not implement the new method, so after this commit `PunicaWrapperNPU` is an abstract class and every `PunicaWrapperNPU(...)` instantiation in `get_punica_wrapper()` (vllm_ascend/platform.py:184) fails with `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class PunicaWrapperNPU with abstract method apply_lora_full_linear`. This breaks ALL LoRA on Ascend, not just the new feature.

Required adaptation in vllm_ascend/lora/punica_npu.py — add `apply_lora_full_linear(self, y, x, weight_stacked, bias_stacked, module_enabled)` to `PunicaWrapperNPU`, mirroring the CPU/XPU implementations (vllm/lora/punica_wrapper/punica_cpu.py / punica_xpu.py): allocate a float32 `adapter_y` of shape (x.size(0), weight_stacked.size(-2)), call the NPU bgmv/sgmv shrink op with `self.bgmv_shrink` (already selected in `__init__` between `vllm_ascend.lora.lora_ops.bgmv_shrink` and `vllm.lora.ops.torch_ops.bgmv_shrink`, passing `[weight_stacked]` and `self.sampler_indices` with scale 1.0), then call the inherited `self._select_full_linear_output(y, adapter_y, bias_stacked, module_enabled)` and do an in-place `y.copy_(result)` (NPU `can_update_inplace()` returns True so the in-place contract in `ClassificationHeadWithLoRA.forward` is preserved). Handle the `self.no_lora` short-circuit and the A2/A3 `_single_lora_slot` path consistently with the existing `add_lora_linear`/`add_lora_logits` implementations. Add a unit test in tests/ut/lora/test_punica_npu.py analogous to the upstream tests/lora tests and existing tests/ut/lora/test_lora.py; extend tests/ut/test_platform.py if it asserts wrapper behavior. No changes are needed for the rest of the commit (LoRAModel.modules_to_save, LoRAFullModuleWeights, model_manager classification-head handling, Pooler.replace_classifier, peft_helper modules_to_save validation) since vllm-ascend uses the upstream LoRA manager, layer registry (`refresh_all_lora_classes` in vllm_ascend/lora/utils.py merely prepends Ascend classes to `_all_lora_classes`), and pooler.
deep_analysis.risk: High if not adapted: enabling `--enable-lora` on Ascend fails at startup on all device types (310P/A2/A3) because `PunicaWrapperNPU` becomes non-instantiable, a regression for existing LoRA users. For the new feature itself: `ClassificationHeadWithLoRA.forward` calls `punica_wrapper.apply_lora_full_linear`, so without a correct NPU implementation sequence-classification `modules_to_save` adapters silently return the base classifier output. The NPU bgmv/sgmv shrink op must accept the stacked full-weight shape `[max_loras, 1, output_size, input_size]` and route rows by `sampler_indices` (request-level, index -1 = no module); `_select_full_linear_output` relies on `sampler_indices` being a device tensor and `torch.where` on NPU, which should work but should be validated on hardware. Also verify the `_single_lora_slot` fast path and `no_lora` handling so the new method matches the existing NPU LoRA routing semantics.

commits.message:
[Bugfix][Mooncake] Report request-level KV load failures under HMA (#56855)

Signed-off-by: NickLucche <nicolo.lucchesi@mistral.ai>

affected_interfaces: vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_connector.py: MooncakeConnector (add get_transfer_results override) and MooncakeConnectorWorker (add _failed_recv_reqs queue + get_transfer_results(); route _mark_failed_recv_request load failures to request-level failed_recving when _is_hma_required)

vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_layerwise_connector.py: MooncakeLayerwiseConnector.get_finished()/get_block_ids_with_load_errors() (currently folds failed recvs into block-level _invalid_block_ids at lines ~1552-1560; must report request-level failed_recving under HMA)

vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake/pull_worker.py: MooncakePullConnectorWorker._mark_request_failed/can_report_invalid_block_ids (silently drops load failures on multi-group layouts; must report failed_recving instead)
vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/sfa_pd_rd2h/connector.py + worker.py: SfaRemoteD2HConnector (block-level failure reporting must be gated to non-HMA)
vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/ascend_multi_connector.py: AscendMultiConnector (inherits MultiConnector.get_transfer_results aggregation; depends on each child reporting failed_recving)
deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: The commit changes the KV-connector failure-reporting contract under HMA (multi-group KV cache): load failures must be reported per-request via KVConnectorTransferResults.failed_recving (returned by get_transfer_results()) instead of block-level invalid_block_ids, and Scheduler._handle_invalid_blocks now raises RuntimeError (fail-closed) if block-level invalid_block_ids are reported on a multi-group layout. vllm-ascend's connectors subclass KVConnectorBase_V1/SupportsHMA and are driven through the shared vllm Scheduler (all custom schedulers subclass vllm Scheduler), so they inherit the new fail-closed path. Adapt by mirroring the upstream Mooncake changes (vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py and store/worker.py): (1) derive _is_hma_required in each worker from `not vllm_config.scheduler_config.disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager and any(not isinstance(g.kv_cache_spec, FullAttentionSpec) for g in kv_cache_config.transfer_groups)`; (2) add a thread-safe failed-recv accumulator (e.g. _failed_recv_reqs queue / _failed_requests set) and branch every load-error reporting path (`_mark_failed_recv_request`, `_report_load_error`, `_mark_request_failed`, oversized-key/partial-get/exception handlers) to enqueue the request id when _is_hma_required, else keep updating invalid_block_ids; (3) add get_transfer_results() on each worker and connector class returning KVConnectorTransferResults(finished_sending, finished_recving, failed_recving) and ensure get_block_ids_with_load_errors() stays empty under HMA so the new RuntimeError is never hit; (4) fix MooncakeLayerwiseConnector.get_finished() to stop folding failed recvs into _invalid_block_ids and instead surface them via failed_recving; (5) add unit tests mirroring test_mooncake_connector_hma.py / test_mooncake_store_worker.py covering the HMA vs non-HMA branches and the scheduler fail-closed behavior.
deep_analysis.risk: Medium. If not adapted, a KV load failure on an HMA model (e.g. DeepSeek V4 / hybrid attention-Mamba layouts) causes a hard RuntimeError in Scheduler._handle_invalid_blocks whenever a connector still reports block-level invalid_block_ids (the older MooncakeConnector and MooncakeLayerwiseConnector paths do this unconditionally), crashing the engine; connectors that already suppress block-level reporting under multi-group (MooncakePullConnector.can_report_invalid_block_ids) instead silently drop failures, leaving requests stuck in WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS without recovery. Additionally, the scheduler no longer performs the hybrid 'recompute whole request' recovery path, so recovery semantics depend entirely on correct failed_recving reporting. vllm-ascend partially mitigates via _validate_kv_load_failure_policy (platform.py:1031) which already forbids recompute policy on hybrid models, but block-level reporting on multi-group is still reachable and would now crash.

affected_interfaces: vllm.v1.utils.CpuGpuBuffer.copy_to_gpu() behavior change (indirectly touches vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py, vllm_ascend/worker/block_table.py, vllm_ascend/worker/dcp_utils.py, spec_decode, sparse_kv_offload — functionally compatible)
deep_analysis.adaptation_guide:
The commit deletes `async_copy_to_gpu` from `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/buffer_utils.py` and folds its behavior into `async_tensor_h2d` in `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py` (which gains optional `device` and a new `out=` destination-tensor parameter). vllm-ascend imports the deleted symbol in 4 files and will raise ImportError once this commit is applied:

1. vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py (line 32 import; call sites 375, 419, 453, 476): change import to `from vllm.utils.torch_utils import async_tensor_h2d` and rename calls. Semantics match: `async_copy_to_gpu(x, device=self.device)` -> `async_tensor_h2d(x, device=self.device)` and `async_copy_to_gpu(npy, out=query_start_loc)` -> `async_tensor_h2d(npy, out=query_start_loc)`. Pay attention to the FIA/ACL-Graph padding path (`_pad_query_start_loc_for_fia` / `_pad_adaptive_query_start_loc_for_fia`) where the copy writes into `self.input_buffers.query_start_loc` via `out=`; the new `out=` path asserts `out.dtype == dtype` (all current uses are int32, so OK).
2. vllm_ascend/worker/v2/pcp_manager.py (line 27 import; call at 299): same rename to `async_tensor_h2d(graph_query_start_loc_np, out=input_buffers.query_start_loc[:graph_num_reqs + 1])`.
3. vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_v2/patch_spec_pp.py (line 6 import; call at 41): rename to `async_tensor_h2d(update_indices, device=pp_handler.device)`.
4. vllm_ascend/_310p/worker/v2/model_runner.py (line 36 import; calls at 194, 215, 237, 1112): same mechanical rename.

Behavioral notes to verify on NPU (NPUPlatform.is_pin_memory_available returns True, so PIN_MEMORY=True):
- The new `async_tensor_h2d` stages a non-pinned CPU tensor into a pinned contiguous CPU buffer via a synchronous `torch.empty(...).copy_(t)` before the non-blocking H2D copy (previously `x.pin_memory()`). Confirm this does not introduce host-device sync stalls in the hot decode path (vLLM CI now detects GPU<->CPU syncs) or break ACL Graph capture.
- `CpuGpuBuffer.copy_to_gpu(n)` now internally calls `cpu.pin_memory()` before the non-blocking copy. vllm-ascend buffers are already allocated with `pin_memory=True` (block_table.py:330, model_runner_v1.py:362, spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py:2157), so `pin_memory()` is a no-op and this is backward-compatible; no change needed, but retest MRV1 decode paths that call `copy_to_gpu`.
- `CpuGpuBuffer.__init__` keeps its `pin_memory` kwarg, so vllm-ascend constructor calls remain valid.

Run the vLLM-ascend worker/model-runner test suites (v2 decode/FULL-graph, PCP, PP spec-decode, 310P) after the swap.
deep_analysis.risk: If not migrated, worker startup fails with ImportError (`cannot import name 'async_copy_to_gpu' from 'vllm.v1.worker.gpu.buffer_utils'`). Beyond the mechanical rename, the new pinning/staging path adds a synchronous CPU copy on every H2D transfer; on Ascend (PIN_MEMORY=True) this runs in the hot decode loop of NPUModelRunnerV2/310P and could introduce GPU<->CPU syncs or ACL Graph capture issues if a source tensor is ever non-contiguous or unpinned. The new `out=` path also hard-asserts `out.dtype == dtype`, so any future vllm-ascend call site with a dtype mismatch (e.g., non-int32 destination) would abort.
